Detector.Details: Detected direct dereference of a JDBC object without a null check. This can lead to a NullPointerException if the Timestamp is null. Ensure that you check for null before dereferencing the object.

BugPattern.ShortDescription: Possible null pointer dereference of JDBC results
BugPattern.Details:
JDBC ResultSet getters that return reference values my return null when the database value is NULL.

Directly invoking a method on the return value can therefore result in a NullPointerException.

Store the value and check for null before dereferencing it where SQL NULL is valid.

Primitive ResultsSet getters (getInt, getLong, getDouble, etc.) are not covered by this rule because they return a default value (0) when the database value is NULL.

MessageCollection.BugCode: Unsafe dereference of JDBC nullable results check.
